subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class per-skill user preference sidecar, and if so should the contract be markdown sidecar, structured `skills.entries.*.config`, or no core support?
rationale: The requested behavior is not implemented, but adding it changes the public skill-loading and prompt-context contract rather than repairing a broken existing contract.

options.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
options.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that loads with the selected skill, is lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, and participates in prompt snapshot and watcher refresh behavior.

options.title: Use structured config only
options.body: Keep user preferences under `skills.entries.*.config` and require individual skills or plugins to interpret them, avoiding new prompt-side markdown composition.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the current model where users maintain a higher-precedence skill override, a separate personal skill, or global context guidance.

recommendation.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that loads with the selected skill, is lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, and participates in prompt snapshot and watcher refresh behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about product/API scope for skills, ClawHub, and core prompt contracts, which recent docs and VISION history point to steipete.
